Condense pep_all to one row per protein and sample

Source: R/prot-all.R
build_prot_all.Rd

Builds the prot_all table behind the 02_prot_all report: for every (protein, Sample) pair, how many ligands it contributes and their summed intensity, plus the protein annotation and any protein-level value the search engine itself reported.

Usage

build_prot_all(
  input,
  protein = c("ProteinFirst", "GeneFirst", "Accession"),
  multi_mapping = c("leading", "all"),
  engine_columns = TRUE
)

Arguments

input

A pep_all-shaped data frame.

protein

Grouping column: "ProteinFirst" (default), "GeneFirst" or "Accession". Which is appropriate depends on the search engine — see the report's methods section.

multi_mapping

"leading" (default) counts each peptide once, for its leading protein; "all" counts it for every protein it maps to, via expand_mapped_proteins(). Under "all" the per-protein peptide counts deliberately no longer sum to the number of peptides in the dataset.

engine_columns

Carry through the protein-level columns the search engine reported (see prot_engine_columns()). Default TRUE.

Value

A data frame with one row per (protein, Sample): Protein, Sample, Condition, BioReplicate, the protein annotation columns present in input, n_Peptides, n_Sequences, n_Peptides_unique, n_Peptides_shared, Area, Log2Area, plus any engine-reported columns. Zero rows, correctly typed, when input has none.

Details

Area is summed on the linear scale within a sample and log2-transformed afterwards, matching build_quant_matrix(). Note that the older get_mat_log2area(pep_all, ProteinFirst, ...) route used by 00_mhc_report and 01_mhc_overview instead averages Log2Area; the two are not interchangeable.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
prot_all <- build_prot_all(pep_short)
build_prot_all(pep_short, protein = "GeneFirst", multi_mapping = "all")
} # }
